title: Slim streaming ergonomics, consolidated retry presets, and credential resilience across SDKs
author: Elena Park
release_notes: Small ergonomics and parity changes across Python/TS/Go SDKs: consolidated retry presets, lightweight streaming surface for pull/push streams, credential fallback mediator and version bumps for all SDKs.
description: Motivation: Multiple SDKs had slightly divergent retry presets and streaming ergonomics that made cross-language feature parity and user documentation inconsistent. This PR consolidates retry presets into a compact, documented set, surfaces a slim streaming facade that is consistent across Python/TypeScript/Go, and adds a credential resilience layer that falls back to configured providers before surfacing errors. Scope: changes are limited to SDK surface layers and small supporting machinery in the SDK packages; runtime platform code is untouched. Key changes include: 1) introduce 'compact' and 'latency-optimized' retry presets with a tiny DSL and mapped defaults in each SDK; 2) implement a thin PullStream / PushStream facade with identical semantics in py/ts/go, including an explicit 'resumeFromCheckpoint' hint and cancellation token hooks; 3) add CredentialMediator that accepts ordered providers and performs soft-fallbacks with telemetry hooks; 4) bump SDK versions: python 2.8.0, typescript 1.17.0, go 1.12.0 and update changelogs; 5) small doc updates and example apps to demonstrate multi-SDK parity. Safety: added test harnesses to exercise retry windows and streaming resume under controlled flakiness. Backwards compatibility: existing constructors are preserved with deprecation warnings for the legacy retry config. Why here: making parity changes in the monorepo ensures we can ship aligned docs and examples at the same time.

review_comments: Marcus Liu: Nice consolidation. Two asks: add explicit note in CHANGELOG about deprecated legacy_retry_config and include an example showing how to migrate. Also please add a small e2e that simulates transient auth failures.
Elena Park: Thanks Marcus, added migration snippet in python/typescript changelogs and a flaky auth test harness under tests/e2e/auth_flaky_sim. Will push shortly.
Priya Singh: The TS PullStream surface looks good but the cancellation semantics need to be deterministic across Node and browser. Can we make cancel() idempotent and document event ordering?
Elena Park: Made cancel() idempotent and added explicit ordering in docs/sdk/streaming.md. Added unit tests covering double-cancel.
Diego Marquez: CI showed intermittent race in Go stream resume; narrowing goroutine handoff and adding small sleep in test fixed it. Consider revisiting production backpressure semantics later.
Elena Park: Acknowledged. Left TODO in code and filed ENG-9611 to follow up on streaming backpressure semantics in runtime.
